subject: P2 response-time exception request — night window backfill plan
messages:
From: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@helixpayments.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: temporary P2 SLA exception for nightly batch window

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. We ran the midnight settlement batch last night and saw repeated P2 escalations (average response latency hitting ~3.5 hours for some reads) across three consecutive runs after the payment rail cold-cache behavior kicked in. Our infra team is scheduling the migration to new caches but it won't land until early June.

Given the business impact and our contract terms, we need to request a temporary waiver of the P2 response-time SLA for the nightly maintenance window (00:00-04:00 PT) for the next three weeks while we finalize the migration. Specifically:
- Current contractual P2 target: response acknowledged within 2 hours
- Requested temporary P2 target for 00:00–04:00 PT: acknowledge within 4 hours, full mitigation within 12 hours

Attached is Helix's incident log and the formal exception request form. Can Redwood provide an operational backfill plan (on-call coverage, escalation path, and provisional credits if needed) so we can keep processing live transactions?

Appreciate fast feedback — our weekend settlement is business-critical.

Thanks,
Dana Ortiz
Head of Payments Operations
Helix Payments
(attachments: helix_incident_log.zip, helix_slo-exception-form.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@helixpayments.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 SLA exception for nightly batch window

Folks — looping you in. Dana flagged recurring late-night P2 breaches tied to cold-cache behavior for Helix. They formally asked for a temporary P2 lift for 00:00–04:00 PT for ~3 weeks while they migrate caches.

Quick summary / asks:
- We can consider a temporary carveout but need an operational mitigations plan from our side (on-call backfill and a tighter escalation path) and clear credit terms.
- Proposed immediate mitigation: activate a paid on-call backfill for the 00:00–04:00 PT window (contractor cover for the next 3 weekends) + an internal fallback model that routes heavy traffic to the warmer model variant during the overnight window.
- I attached a draft backfill roster CSV (proposed_oncall_backfill.csv) and the Helix exception form.

Sooj and Ben — can you estimate the cost implication for contractor backfill and confirm we can enable routing to the warmer model variant without production risk?
Laura — need your guidance on commercial credits and whether we can offer a one-off SLA credit if breaches happen during the approved window.

If we can get sign-off today I will reply to Helix with the plan and a timeline.

— Marcus
Engineering Manager, Runtime Team
Redwood Inference
(attachments: proposed_oncall_backfill.csv, helix_slo-exception-form.pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-20T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 SLA exception for nightly batch window

On Thu, May 20, 2026 at 11:03 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — looping you in. Dana flagged recurring late-night P2 breaches tied to cold-cache behavior for Helix.

Agenda-level technical take: enabling the warmer model variant is low-risk for short windows; the main operational gap is overnight human response. We can do the routing flip in a controlled canary (2 hosts) then roll to full overnight traffic.

Operational proposal (detail):
1) Contractor backfill for 00:00–04:00 PT on weekends (Fri/Sat/Sun local) for 3 weeks: 2 contractors per night with runbook access and escalation rights.
2) Internal on-call augmentation: rotate a senior engineer (Mateo) as on-call lead for the first 2 weeks to shadow contractors and own tie-breaker decisions.
3) Escalation path: contractor -> Mateo (on-call lead) -> Marcus (Runtime EM) -> Ben (Head of Support) -> Laura (Sales Ops for credits/contract exceptions).
4) Monitoring: create a dedicated dashboard and PagerDuty schedule for this temporary roster; alerts to include SLO percentage drop and sustained 90th/95th percentile latency spikes.

I estimate the contractor cost at ~USD 8k/week; cost to run the warmer variant is negligible for the short window. I can spin up the pager schedule and dash if we approve.

— Soojin
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@helixpayments.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 SLA exception for nightly batch window

Thanks team — this looks reasonable. A few notes: 
- Approve the operational plan (contractor backfill + Mateo as lead + routing to warmer model) as a short-term mitigation.
- From the support/contract side: we can approve an explicit temporary SLA amendment (P2 4-hour window overnight) conditional on Helix acknowledging the exception and signing the exception form.
- Credit policy: propose a capped credit equivalent to 2 days of hosting fees per each week where a breach occurs during the approved window. Laura, please confirm if that aligns with our standard practice for similar carveouts.

Marcus — once Laura confirms the credit formulation I authorize you to send the official plan to Helix and kick off the contractor hires.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Support
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@helixpayments.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 SLA exception for nightly batch window — Approved terms

Thanks — reviewing the proposed terms now. To be explicit:
- We approve the temporary P2 target change to 4 hours for 00:00–04:00 PT for a three-week period (2026-05-22 through 2026-06-12), pending signed exception form from Helix.
- Credit model: capped credit of up to 2 days hosting fees per week with a hard cap of 6 days total across the three-week period. Credits apply only to breaches that occur inside the approved 00:00–04:00 PT window and while the approved backfill roster is active.
- Operational requirements for approval: contractor roster loaded into PagerDuty, Mateo assigned as on-call lead with escalation rights, and the routing-canary executed before the first night window.

Marcus — please send the formal exception response to Dana (copy legal if Helix signs) and attach the exception form with the exact dates. Once we have the signed form, we will trigger contractor onboarding and pager schedules.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
